headline: Huawei's chairman says its Ascend AI chips have likely overtaken Nvidia in China, but supply cannot meet demand.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered to 5: a company claim on market share that cannot be independently checked.
importance_line: What changed: Huawei says its chips have likely overtaken Nvidia's in China, which matters to Chinese AI developers and buyers who face short supply; this is Huawei's own claim, Nvidia's share is hard to measure and no outside figure is given.
summary: ijiwei reports, as relayed by TrendForce, that Huawei's rotating chairman Eric Xu said at the Huawei Connect conference in Shanghai that Ascend AI chips have likely overtaken Nvidia in China, based on data Huawei can track. He also said Huawei is selling every chip it can make, that domestic demand still far exceeds supply, and that it has no plan for a broad overseas rollout, so Chinese customers come first.
notes: Read on TrendForce (full text), which relays ijiwei; ijiwei original not opened. Chunk source digitimes gave a teaser only. Score 5, WATCHLIST, still inside the report cutoff of 5 and up.
